docRequirement: admin-setup.md:45 binds us to FOUR managed-settings sources checked "in priority order" with "the first one that returns a non-empty configuration" applied: Server-managed (Highest), plist/registry policy (High: macOS `com.anthropic.claudecode` plist, Windows `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode`), File-based managed (Medium), Windows user registry `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode` (Lowest) — table at :47-52. The same line binds the cross-source lock keys (honoured when ANY admin-controlled source sets them, HKCU excluded per server-managed-settings.md:141). :60 states the property the High tier exists for: "The plist and HKLM registry locations work with any provider and resist tampering because they require admin privileges to write", while HKCU "is writable without elevation, so treat it as a convenience default rather than an enforcement channel". :62 and :74 make `wslInheritsWindowsSettings: true` deployable only from HKLM or the Program Files file, and :75 names the `/status` channel strings `(HKLM)` and `(file)`.
current: We implement the arbitration RULE correctly over exactly TWO of the four sources. `ManagedPolicySourcesV1` declares only `delivered` and `file` (packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:98-110), and `composeManagedPolicySources` is priority-order-first-non-empty-wins over that pair — delivered wins wholesale iff `carriesManagedSettings(delivered)` (:184-198), with the documented cross-source carve-out for `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` and the sandbox network lock (:201-205). The module docblock states the two-source set as the whole documented set: "We have exactly two, and they are the two the documentation names" (:4). `ManagedPolicyWinnerV1 = 'delivered' | 'file' | 'none'` (:130). Upstream, `EnforcedManagedPolicySeams` exposes exactly two seams, `file` and `delivered` (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:53-58), and `resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy` feeds only those into the composition (:127-139); nothing supplies a third. The file channel is the rebranded Medium tier: `/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json`, `/etc/nessy/managed-policy.json`, `%ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:44-52) plus the `managed-policy.d/` drop-in dir (:62-67), read under a host-owned regime (:229-264). That regime is POSIX-only: `assertPosixOwnerAndMode` returns immediately on win32 (:78-81), so on Windows the only managed channel we have is read with no ownership or ACL check at all. Diagnostics follow the two sources: `WINNER_LABEL` has three entries, `Managed settings (remote)` / `(file)` / `No managed settings source is in effect` (packages/shared/src/config/config-doctor.ts:231-235, rendered at :426), `shadowedManagedFileWarning` fires only for `winner === 'delivered' && fileCarriesSettings` (:253-264), and the CLI emits the raw label as `managedSource` (apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:188). Absence is verified binary-safe: `grep -ran -E "HKLM|HKCU|HKEY_LOCAL|HKEY_CURRENT|SOFTWARE.Policies|CFPreferences|com\.anthropic\.claudecode|managed-preferences|plist|defaults read|reg query|systemPreferences|winreg" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' packages apps` (dist/ and node_modules excluded) returns only prose comments (managed-composition.ts:29 and :44, config-doctor.ts:12), an unrelated MachineGuid `reg query` in packages/shared/src/credentials/backends/secure-storage.ts:105, an Info.plist dock-icon comment at apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:428, and an Electron mock's API-name list at apps/electron/testing/electron-mock-preload.ts:53. No `plist`/`winreg`/registry dependency appears in any package.json.
divergence: The rule is right; the source SET is short by two, and the two missing ones are the tamper-resistant tier and the convenience tier. Absent: (a) the High-priority OS policy channel — macOS managed-preferences plist and `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\<product>` — which the doc places ABOVE the file channel we do have, and (b) the Lowest-priority `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\<product>` tier. This is not a key-name mismatch: there is no reader, no seam and no winner label for either, so nothing in the pipeline could carry them even if a value existed. Two consequences ride along. First, the doc gives the High tier its own property — admin-privilege-only writes — and we satisfy that only on POSIX, via file ownership; on Windows the fork has no ownership/ACL check on any managed source (managed-policy-loader.ts:79 early-returns for win32), so it currently has no tamper-resistant managed channel at all. Second, `wslInheritsWindowsSettings` (admin-setup.md:62, :74) has no deployable home, since both of its documented sources are the Windows halves of the missing tier plus a Program Files file we place under `%ProgramData%` instead. The cross-source carve-out's HKCU exclusion is satisfied only vacuously. `policyHelper`, the fifth preempting source named on the same page (:54), is a SEPARATE finding (f109/f027) and is deliberately not folded in here.

change.what: New module, sibling to managed-policy-loader.ts, returning the same `ManagedPiPolicyLoadV1` shape. darwin: read the managed-preferences domain (the Nessy analogue of `com.anthropic.claudecode` — pick the bundle id already used by apps/electron packaging and record the choice, since the doc's identifier is Claude-branded and our file paths are already rebranded to Nessy). win32: read `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Nessy` for the admin tier and `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Nessy` for the user tier. Both must funnel through the existing `parseManagedPiPolicyTolerantV1` with a `source` string naming the domain/key, so refused entries become `ManagedPolicyDropV1`s the doctor already knows how to print, and both must be TOLERANT: an absent domain/key is the normal case and returns `DEFAULT_MANAGED_PI_POLICY` with no drop, never a throw. Inject the OS read behind a dependency like `ManagedPiPolicyLoaderDependencies` does (a `readOsPolicy?: () => unknown` seam) so tests need no real registry or plist. Decide and document the value encoding — the page specifies the LOCATION but not how a nested settings object is represented in registry values.

change.symbol: ManagedPolicySourcesV1, ManagedPolicyWinnerV1, composeManagedPolicySources, composeNetworkLock, module docblock
change.what: Widen `ManagedPolicySourcesV1` (:98-110) from `{delivered, file}` to the four documented tiers, e.g. `{delivered, osPolicy, file, userRegistry}`. Replace the hand-written two-way branch in `composeManagedPolicySources` (:184-198) with an ordered array `[['delivered',delivered],['osPolicy',os],['file',file],['userRegistry',user]]` and pick the first whose `carriesManagedSettings` is true — the semantics are unchanged for the existing two, so this is a generalisation, not a behaviour change. Widen `ManagedPolicyWinnerV1` (:130) to `'delivered' | 'plist' | 'hklm' | 'file' | 'hkcu' | 'none'` (plist and hklm are distinct labels because admin-setup.md:75 names `(HKLM)` as a user-visible `/status` string). `composeNetworkLock` (:163-174) and the `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` fold (:201-205) must union across every ADMIN-controlled source but EXCLUDE `userRegistry` (server-managed-settings.md:141, restated at admin-setup.md:45) — today they take one `other`, so they need to take a list. Rewrite the docblock at :2-10 and the sentence at :44 ("excludes the user-writable HKCU tier, which we do not have"), which will be false once the tier exists.

Add `osPolicy?: () => ManagedPiPolicyLoadV1` and `userRegistry?: () => ManagedPiPolicyLoadV1` to the seams (:53-58) defaulting to the new loaders, and pass all four into `composeManagedPolicySources` at :132. `drops` at :135 currently forwards only `file.drops` — concatenate the drops of every source that produced them so a malformed registry/plist entry is reported with its own source string. `fileCarriesSettings` (:137) stays as-is; add the sibling flags the diagnostics need (see config-doctor).

Extend `WINNER_LABEL` (:231-235) with `plist: 'Managed settings (plist)'`, `hklm: 'Managed settings (HKLM)'`, `hkcu: 'Managed settings (HKCU)'` — the map is a total `Record<ManagedPolicyWinnerV1, string>`, so widening the type makes this a compile error rather than a silent gap, which is the desired failure. Generalise `shadowedManagedFileWarning` (:253-264): its `winner !== 'delivered'` guard encodes the two-source world; with four tiers ANY higher-priority winner shadows ANY lower source that carries settings, so it needs the winner plus the set of carrying sources, and `ConfigDoctorInputV1.fileCarriesSettings` (:73) generalises to per-source flags.

No code change required — `managedSource: input.winner` passes the label straight through — but its JSON value domain grows from three strings to six. Note it wherever the doctor JSON shape is documented; fleet scripts matching on `"delivered"|"file"|"none"` will silently miss the new values.

Table-driven: one case proving the documented order (a lower tier carrying settings loses to every higher tier that carries settings), and one negative proving an EMPTY higher tier does not shadow a lower non-empty one (`carriesManagedSettings` false ⇒ skip). Plus one cross-source case proving the sandbox lock unions from delivered/osPolicy/file but NOT from userRegistry.

Cover the new loaders through their injected read seam: absent domain/key ⇒ default policy, no drop; malformed entry ⇒ tolerant drop carrying the domain/key as `source`; valid entry ⇒ parsed policy. No real registry or plist in tests.

blastRadius: `composeManagedPolicySources` has 4 callers, all in packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts, covered by packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/managed-composition.test.ts. `resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy` has 8 callers across apps/cli/src/doctor.ts, managed-policy-resolution.ts (retention provider at :167, doctor input at :281) and packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts, covered by packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/config-doctor-input.test.ts and storage-runtime-delivered-policy.test.ts; packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/managed-policy-reread.test.ts re-reads policy per session. `ManagedPolicyWinnerV1` crosses a package boundary (shared → server-core → apps/cli) and its value LEAVES the process as the `managedSource` field of the doctor JSON at apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:188 — an output/wire boundary a fleet check can be matching on, so widening the union is a compatibility change, not a local refactor. `WINNER_LABEL` is a total record, so the type change breaks the build until every label exists (intentional). The composed policy governs permissions, sandbox network/filesystem, the `availableModels` allowlist, plugin mandates and `cleanupPeriodDays` — a new higher-priority source can therefore change enforcement AND, through retention, cause deletions no administrator intended, which is the repo's stated risk trigger for permission decisions plus destructive sweeps. It also adds platform-specific OS I/O to a startup path that today only touches the filesystem: the read must be seam-injected and must fail soft, because a throw here reaches process start. No new persistence WRITE; the plist/registry are read-only inputs. `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts` (`MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS`, `refuseUnknownKeys`) is reused unchanged — the new sources carry the same key set, so no schema change. `docs-site/` must gain the MDM/GPO deployment locations, since an administrator cannot discover a registry key or plist domain from the app.
userImpact: For the deployment path the fork actually documents — the `managed-policy.json` file plus drop-ins, or the gateway-delivered payload — none observable; policy applies exactly as expected. It surfaces the moment an administrator uses standard OS tooling. On macOS, an MDM configuration profile / managed-preferences payload (the normal way a bank ships desktop policy) binds to nothing: the app reads no preference domain, so the profile installs cleanly, changes nothing, and `nessy-general-agent doctor` prints "No managed settings source is in effect" — a deployed, verified-by-MDM policy that is silently inert, with no error anywhere to explain it. On Windows, Group Policy is likewise a no-op, and there is a sharper edge: the one managed channel Windows does have, `%ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json`, is read with the ownership/mode check skipped entirely (managed-policy-loader.ts:79), so the fork has no channel with the admin-write-only property admin-setup.md:60 attributes to the plist/HKLM tier — a user who can write that path can rewrite managed policy and there is no higher-priority source that could override it. WSL sessions inherit nothing, because `wslInheritsWindowsSettings` has no admin-only Windows source to be deployed from.
notes: Every cited line was read verbatim this session (managed-composition.ts 1-213, managed-policy-loader.ts 1-20/69-264/274-387, managed-policy-resolution.ts 16-58/124-139/193-337, config-doctor.ts 1-60/224-275/426-438 via grep, apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:188 via grep, admin-setup.md 1-90 from a fresh `curl -sL`). Three things I could NOT verify and that the implementer must settle. (1) The default ACL on `%ProgramData%\Nessy` — I proved the loader performs no check on win32, not that the directory is user-writable in practice; the tamper-resistance claim is about what our code enforces, and the actual ACL depends on what the installer sets. (2) The registry value encoding: admin-setup.md gives the KEY path but not how a nested settings object (e.g. `sandbox.network.allowedDomains`) is represented in registry values; settings.md may specify it, and it should be read before the loader is written rather than invented. (3) The Nessy-side identifiers — the page's `com.anthropic.claudecode` and `...\Policies\ClaudeCode` are Claude-branded; the fork rebranded the file paths to Nessy, so the analogue names are a product decision (I did not confirm which bundle id apps/electron ships). `policyHelper` (admin-setup.md:54) is tracked separately as f109/f027 and is intentionally excluded from this spec; note only that once it exists it preempts all four, which is why the composition should be generalised to an ordered LIST rather than to four hard-coded fields.
